vi: đứng đầu / người đứng đầu / xuất sắc / vạm vỡ

en: immortal soul, i.e. that can be detached from the body
note: Phonosemantic compound. 鬼 represents the meaning and 云 represents the sound. Simplified form of 䰟.

vi: linh hồn; hồn phách (tức là gắn liền với cơ thể)
en: mortal soul, i.e. attached to the body
note: Phonosemantic compound. 鬼 represents the meaning and 白 represents the sound.

note: Phonosemantic compound. 鬼 represents the meaning and 麻 represents the sound.
Simplified form of 魚.  Pictograph of a fish.

en: Shandong Province 山東省|山东省[Shān​dōng​Shěng]
vassal state during the Zhou Dynasty (1066-221 BC) in modern day Shandong Province
note: Simplified form of 魯.  Phonosemantic compound. 甘 represents the meaning and 魚 represents the sound. Based on the original meaning "tasty". The current meaning is a phonetic loan.
Phonosemantic compound. 鱼 represents the meaning and 羊 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鮮.
Phonosemantic compound. 鱼 represents the meaning and 京 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鯨.
Phonosemantic compound. 鱼 represents the meaning and 卢 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鱸.
Simplified form of 鳥.  Pictograph of a bird.
Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 九 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鳩.

Simplified form of 鳳.  Phonosemantic compound. 鳥 represents the meaning and 凡 represents the sound. Originally a pictograph of a mythical Chinese bird, similar to a phoenix. Later the phonetic component 凡 was added.
Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 夗 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鴛.

en: (bound form, used in the names of birds of various biological families)

note: Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 央 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鴦.
Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 江 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鴻.
Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 我 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鵝.
Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 武 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鵡.

comps.t: Depicts marching (止) with a weapon (戈).

note: Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 朋 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鵬.
Simplified form of 鵲.  Phonosemantic compound. 鳥 represents the meaning and 昔 represents the sound. Originally written as 舄.

en: oriole or various birds of the Sylvidae family including warblers

note: Phonosemantic compound. 鸟 represents the meaning and 䧹 represents the sound. Simplified form of 鷹.
Pictograph of a deer.
Phonosemantic compound. 鹿 represents the meaning and 其 represents the sound.
Simplified form of 麗.  Pictograph of a deer (鹿) with two beautiful antlers. The traditional component 鹿 was removed for simplification.

vi: hươu xạ (Moschus moschiferus) / còn gọi là 香獐子
note: Phonosemantic compound. 鹿 represents the meaning and 射 represents the sound.
Simplified form of 麥.  The top component 來 is a pictograph of wheat. It is unclear why the foot component (夂) was added to the character for "wheat".

vi: biến thể cũ của 麵|面[mian4]
biến thể của 麻[ma2] / cây gai
en: generic name for hemp, flax etc
hemp or flax fiber for textile materials

note: Phonosemantic compound. 么 represents the meaning and 麻 represents the sound. Variant form of 麼.

Simplified form of 黃.  Pictograph of a person with a person with a large belly, representing someone deformed. Based on the original meaning "physically impaired". Later meaning shifted to "yellow; sallow", a skin color associated with illness.

vi: nhóm dân tộc Li ở tỉnh Hải Nam / họ [Li2] / viết tắt của Li-băng 黎巴嫩[Li2 ba1 nen4]
viết tắt của tỉnh Hắc Long Giang 黑龍江|黑龙江[Hei1 long2 jiang1]
note: Pictograph of a person whose face has been tattooed. In ancient China criminals were punished by having their faces permanently marked. Later writers reanalyzed the character as a chimney being blackened by fire, so the bottom component was changed to look like 炎 (flame).

vi: im lặng / viết từ trí nhớ

note: Simplified form of 點.

vi: vạc nấu cổ có hai quai và ba hoặc bốn chân / nồi (phương ngữ) / bước vào một giai đoạn (văn cổ) / bộ Khang Hy số 206 / một trong 64 quẻ của Kinh Dịch

to enter upon a period of (classical)
one of the 64 hexagrams of the Book of Changes
note: Pictograph of an ancient cooking pot with two handles and three or four legs.
Simplified form of 齊.  Pictograph of stalks of millet. Possibly alludes to the even and uniform appearance of a millet field.
Simplified form of 齒.  Pictograph of a mouth full of teeth. The sound component 止 was added later.
Pictograph of a dragon curled up. The simplified character 龙 was adapted from the cursive form of the traditional character 龍.
